title: NVTX prefetch shadowwave timeline notes
body:
Context and motivation:
We keep seeing intermittent tail spikes (~95th-99th percentile) in mixed-length decode workloads when CUDA graph replay is enabled. Nsight captures show recurring short windows where SM occupancy drops sharply for a subset of kernels while other kernels remain nominally busy. This doc collects NVTX-tagged traces, quick hypotheses, and a small set of reproducible experiments we ran on the staging cluster (A100s, 40GB).

High-level summary (tl;dr):
- Observed a reproducible pattern we call 'prefetch shadowwave' — a short, recurring phase where async prefetch + cuda-graph replays produce transient memory bandwidth contention and launch jitter that reduces effective SM occupancy for attention kernels.
- Reducing prefetch window from 8MB->2MB or switching off graph-capture for the first N warm iterations removes the shadowwave and cuts 99th latency by ~18–24% on the test workload.
- Temporary mitigation: adaptive prefetch throttle + minimal cuda-graph warmup. Need follow-ups to generalize and integrate into the runtime heuristics.

Experiment setup:
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100-SXM4 40GB (driver 535.XX), CUDA 12.2, Nsight Systems 2029.4.
- Model: decoder-only 7B quantized (q4), sequence length distribution: 8% long (>1024), 72% short (<=128), remaining mid.
- Workload: production-like mixed batches with continuous KV-cache activity and occasional mid-request reranks.
- Runtime flags: continuous-batching=enabled, kv-cache-prefetch=async, cuda-graph=enabled (graph-replay warmup=5).
- Instrumentation: NVTX ranges around prefetch start/end, cudaGraphCaptureStart/End, kernel launch NVTX for key kernels (attn, ff, norm), and host-side timestamps. Traces uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-traces/prefetch-shadowwave/2029-11-07/*

Representative commands:
- Start trace (nsys): nsys profile --sample=none --trace=nvtx,cuda --output=shadowwave-20291107 \
  --capture-range=nvtx:prefetch_start,nvtx:prefetch_end --target-processes=all --force-overwrite true -- python run_infer.py --mix-batch

- CUDA graph warmup patch (local test):
  - Capture only after warmup iterations: set env CUDA_GRAPH_WARMUP=10
  - Prefetch throttle: PREFETCH_WINDOW_BYTES=2097152 (2MB) / default was 8388608 (8MB)

What the Nsight timelines show (notes from trace scans):
- Pattern: repeated burst every ~120–180ms where host-side prefetch NVTX begins, we see a flurry of async DMA copies (cudaMemcpyAsync) overlapping with cudaGraph launches.
- Immediately following the DMA burst, the attention kernel launches become more sparse in time (gaps of 0.6–1.2ms) compared to baseline (0.08–0.2ms).
- SM active warps drop ~20–35% during the shadowwave window; achieved occupancy reported by driver/utilization charts falls from ~78% -> ~48% for attention kernels.
- KV-cache related kernels (prefetch consumers) show increased L2 read stalls and DRAM util spikes, suggesting memory bus contention.
- When cuda-graph capture happens across the prefetch window (i.e., graph captured while DMA in-flight), replay tends to repeat the alignment mismatch, amplifying the effect.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Prefetch DMA bursts create short-lived DRAM/L2 congestion that increases load latency for attention kernels, reducing warp throughput (dominant).
2) CUDA graph capture and replay capture host->device timing such that kernel launch batching aligns with prefetch windows, creating persistent gaps on replay.
3) Stream priority interactions: prefetch running on non-priority stream gets less scheduler attention during replay, causing kernel serialization.

Quick tests and results:
- Test A: Lowered prefetch window to 2MB (PREFETCH_WINDOW_BYTES=2MB)
  - Result: 99th latency down by 18%, SM occupancy dips reduced to 10–12% from 20–35%. Trace: prefetch DMA still visible but smaller and less overlapping with attn launches.

- Test B: Disable cuda-graph capture for first 20 iterations, then enable
  - Result: 99th latency down by 22%. Nsight: initial traces show prefetch and kernel launches de-correlated; after graphs enabled, less persistent synchronization artifact.

- Test C: Move prefetch to a higher-priority stream
  - Result: marginal improvement (~6% 99th). Suggests stream priority helps but doesn't fully solve the contention from memory subsystem.

Quantitative snippets (median across 10 runs):
- Baseline (8MB prefetch, graph warmup=5): p50=43ms, p95=121ms, p99=218ms
- Prefetch 2MB: p50=42ms, p95=105ms, p99=179ms
- Warmup 20 (no-capture initial): p50=41ms, p95=98ms, p99=170ms

Trace examples and discussion:
- shadowwave-20291107-run3.nsys: shows tight alignment between cudaGraphLaunch and the largest DMA spikes. NVTX markers: [prefetch_start] at T, then two cudaMemcpyAsync ranges, then [cuda_graph_capture] ended at T+6ms -> replaying this graph reliably reproduces the T-aligned gaps.
- shadowwave-20291107-run7.nsys: after changing PREFETCH_WINDOW, DMA spikes are smaller and interleaving is gentler; attn kernels overlap with DMA but without the launch-silence windows.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Is the effect materially worse on multi-GPU NVLink configs? We only tested single GPU. Suggest a 2-GPU NVLink run to check for nvlink-prefetch coherence issues.
- How does quantization degree modulate DMA size/shape? Larger dtype => less DMA but different kernel durations; may change alignment.
- Can we improve capture logic to detect in-flight DMA (via streamQuery) and defer capture end until quiet? Proof-of-concept: add a small post-capture barrier when recent async copies exceed threshold.

Operational mitigations (short-term):
- Add runtime knob prefetched_bytes_limit with default lowered for mixed-length workloads.
- Add an option to delay first cuda-graph capture until N stable iterations (configurable).
- Expose stream-priority toggle in Dedicated profiles when prefetch active.

Longer-term changes to consider:
- Capture-aware prefetch scheduling: runtime observes when graph capture is happening and pinpoints safe windows for prefetch to minimize overlap.
- Adaptive prefetch sizing per-request based on observed DRAM latency and L2 miss rates.
- Kernel launch coalescing improvements that avoid aligning launches to DMA bursts on replay (introduce micro-random jitter during capture).

Notes to reviewers:
- Traces are under s3 link in linked_artifacts (internal). Please look at run3 and run7 for the clear before/after.
- Related tickets: INF-2741 (investigate prefetch tail spikes), INF-2810 (cuda-graph warmup heuristic).
- Quick patch with PREFETCH_WINDOW_BYTES environment toggle is in PR 842. The PR is intentionally simple to validate the hypothesis; it should not be shipped as-is for GA.

Next steps (owners):
- Ravi: run 2-GPU NVLink reproduction and post traces (target by 2029-11-14).
- June: prototype post-capture quiet-wait heuristic and measure warmup cost (target by 2029-11-12).
- Me (Ava): synthesize a small bench that varies dtype/seq distribution to map the parameter space and produce a recommended default prefetch size (target by 2029-11-15).

TODO (short):
- Add microbench that toggles stream priority and measure scheduling latency per-kernel.
- Formalize the metric we use to detect a 'shadowwave' (SM occupancy drop >15% sustained for >2ms).
- Add a unit test that simulates prefetch spikes during capture to verify heuristics.

Appendix: quick NVTX tags used in these traces
- nvtx:prefetch_start / nvtx:prefetch_end
- nvtx:cuda_graph_capture_start / nvtx:cuda_graph_capture_end
- nvtx:kernel:attn:launch / nvtx:kernel:ff:launch / nvtx:kernel:norm:launch

Appendix: config knobs used in experiments
- PREFETCH_WINDOW_BYTES (int bytes)
- CUDA_GRAPH_WARMUP (iterations)
- PREFETCH_STREAM_PRIORITY (low|normal|high)
- CONTINUOUS_BATCHING_ENABLED (true|false)

If you want raw timelines/NSYS captures, ping me on #eng-runtime and I will drop links or upload the nsys files privately.

-- Ava

(End of draft)
